plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no incentive to shade my bid down, and bidding higher than my value risks negative profit. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $25.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a private value of $18, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $18, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay less than my value when I do win.
